content.text:
I read through `0.html` and made no changes: I couldn't find anything that would be a clear improvement rather than a matter of taste. I checked by reading only; nothing was rendered in a browser or run through a validator.

## What I checked

- **Document head:** the markup is valid, and `lang`, charset, viewport, `color-scheme` and the empty favicon are all in place.
- **Spacing rules:** the heading, section, `hgroup` and `:last-child` margin rules resolve in the right order, with no specificity conflicts.
- **Overflow:** long words, `pre`, tables, media and form controls are all contained or scroll.
- **Layout direction and insets:** logical properties are used throughout, and the safe-area padding is correct.
- **Print:** the print styles undo the screen-only choices (table display, `pre` wrapping, closed `details`, link URLs).

## Changes that depend on what you want

| Option | Trade-off |
|---|---|
| Add `<meta name="description">` and a real `<title>` | Needs actual content; "0" is a placeholder I'd only be guessing at |
| Wrap tables in a scrolling `<div tabindex="0">` instead of `table { display: block }` | Better keyboard and screen-reader behaviour, but requires wrapper markup on every table |
| Differentiate `h4`/`h5`/`h6` | They currently all render as 1rem bold; only matters if you nest that deep |
| Use `max-inline-size: 65ch` instead of `40rem` | Slightly shorter line length; purely a matter of preference |
| Add `@page { margin: 2cm }` | Consistent print margins, but overrides the user's browser default |

If you tell me what the page is for (real content, a reusable starter template, smallest possible size), I can make targeted changes. Any of the options above are quick to apply if you want them.
